title: Sachem's Neck
summary: A Shelter Island placename connected to Native leadership, family movement, and Mashomuck history.
history_content: The name is connected not to a local Shelter Island sachem, but to Ambusco, described in a 1675 record as a late sachem of Southold who received permission to move with his family to Shelter Island. The place is associated with the broader Mashomuck/Shelter Island Native landscape.
translation_content:
Sachem is an adopted English form of an Algonquian title for a chief. Related words in Narragansett, Delaware, Abnaki, and Chippewa carry meanings connected with being a chief.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place-names – as carriers of history, tradition and emotions, and with their significant symbolic value – have an extremely important part to play.”

— Leif Nilsson, Staffan Nyström and Annette C. Torensjö, Good Place-Name Practice (2019), PDF page 49
preservation_content: Sachem's Neck preserves a record of Native movement, permission, and refuge on Shelter Island after colonial settlement reshaped Southold and nearby communities.
